brls:Header.title: There's a game that isn't appearing in the game list.

brls:Label.text: Only games that you created a folder for (named with the game's title ID) will appear in the game list.
Make sure you named the folder you created in step 1 in the 'Setup' section correctly. Make sure the folder's name really is the correct title ID for that game.

brls:Header.title: I named each game's folder as the title ID, but they were somehow renamed to also have the game's name. Why? Will this break anything?

brls:Label.text: No, that's expected.
After starting the app, it will rename any game folders it can to also have the game's name. This is just for making it easier to know which ID belongs to which game when adding mods.
Everything will work as long as the title ID in the parenthesis isn't changed.

brls:Header.title: After enabling a mod, I don't notice it in the game.

brls:Label.text: Disable the mod in the app. In the settings, turn on the moved file dialog setting. Then try enabling the mod again. You'll see a report listing the files moved.

Make sure the folders and files are all named correctly. The first folder in the path listed should be the folder you put directly in the `mod_alchemy/[-GAME-NAME-] ([-TITLE-ID-])/[-GROUP-NAME-]/[-THING-BEING-MODDED-]/[-MOD-NAME-]/` folder. It should usually be named `romfs`. `romfs` should contain more folders matching the game's file system.

If everything looks fine there, try a file explorer. Go to that mod's folder in `mod_alchemy/[-GAME-NAME-] ([-TITLE-ID-])/[-GROUP-NAME-]/[-THING-BEING-MODDED-]/[-MOD-NAME-]/`. If it really is enabled, it should be empty with all folders and files moved to `/atmosphere/contents/[-TITLE-ID-]/`.

brls:Header.title: A mod is only being partially enabled. Not all files belonging to that mod are being used.

brls:Label.text: Disable the mod in the app. In the settings, turn on the moved file dialog setting. Then try enabling the mod again. You'll see a report listing the files that were moved.

If you see some of the mod's files and folders not listed, it's likely they aren't being moved because of a file conflict. There may already be a file within `/atmosphere/contents/[-GAME-TITLE-ID-]/` with the same name and location as a file that's not being moved from within `mod_alchemy/[-GAME-NAME-] ([-TITLE-ID-])/[-GROUP-NAME-]/[-THING-BEING-MODDED-]/[-MOD-NAME-]/`.
If you really want the mod to be fully enabled, you will need to find out where the conflicting file came from. It may have come from another mod that was enabled through the app.

Try using 'Disable All Mods' in the app. Then try searching your SD card for that file's name. You should be able to see all the mods that use it. If some of those mods may have been enabled at the same time, that would've been the problem. You will need to try to sort out the conflicting files between them.

If the file is still located within `/atmosphere/contents/[-GAME-TITLE-ID-]/` even after disabling all mods through the app, then that file does not belong to any of the mods in Simple Mod Alchemist. It was put there manually, so you will need to figure out why it's there and if you need it.
Once the conflicting files are sorted out, the mod should enable fully.

brls:Header.title: The menu options are weird or messed up. Maybe I'm seeing an option named 'romfs' in the menu.

brls:Label.text: The folder structure in the 'mod_alchemy' folder is probably not set up correctly.

If you tried enabling any mods in the menu (or if you're not sure if you did), first use the 'Disable All Mods' option in the game's options menu to fix any folders or files that may have been improperly moved from the 'mod_alchemy' folder.
Review steps 2-6 in the installation instructions.

Make sure all the mods are set up in the following manner in the following folder structure: 'mod_alchemy/[-GAME-NAME-] ([-TITLE-ID-])/[-GROUP-NAME-]/[-THING-BEING-MODDED-]/[-MOD-NAME-]/romfs/[ MOD FOLDERS AND FILES HERE ]`

brls:Header.title: Everything froze for a long time when I tried to enable a mod.

brls:Label.text: This can happen if a mod consists of a really large number files (even if those files are tiny).

Wait for it to finish. Interrupting it could corrupt your mods or even your SD card, and then you would need to restore it from a backup. It may take up to 10 minutes if the mod consists of over 1,000 files.
Using such large mods (such as mod packs) is slow at the moment. It would be better to split the mod pack into smaller, individual mods that would be comprised of under ~100 files.

brls:Header.title: When using the app, it closed abruptly, claiming it closed from an error.

brls:Label.text: See if it continues to happen.
If it was working fine at one point, but suddenly this issue began happening, try restoring from a backup if you have one. See the 'Backing Up' section.

If it still continues to be a problem, feel free to file a GitHub Issue for this app. In it, describe how you came across the error, how the folders that contain the related mod are organized (if it was related to a specific mod), and any other details you think may be helpful.

brls:Header.title: I want to remove the app and all mods it is using from my SD card.

brls:Label.text: For each game in app's game list, run the 'Disable All Mods' option before you delete anything.
Only after doing so, delete the 'mod_alchemy' folder from the root of your SD card, along with the Simple Mod Alchemist app file from the 'switch' directory.

brls:Header.title: I want to remove the app and all mods it is using from my SD card, but I can't access the 'Disable All Mods' option in the app for some reason.

brls:Label.text: You'll need to manually handle the mod files. Please see the 'Advanced' section.

brls:Header.title: I want to have a mod always in use, and I don't want to set it up in this app. Will the app still work fine if I just put its files under '/atmosphere/contents/[-GAME-TITLE-ID-]/'?

brls:Label.text: The app will only touch its own mod files (including those that it moved into the '/atmosphere/contents/[-GAME-TITLE-ID-]/' folder).

brls:Header.title: How does the app handle conflicts between files?

brls:Label.text: If it tries to enable a mod that uses files that another mod is already using (whether that other mod is managed by Simple Mod Alchemist or not), the mod will be enabled to the best extent it can be, but any conflicting files will not be used. The other mod's files will remain in use.
The app only moves non-conflicting files belonging to the mod being enabled. Whatever files are currently in '/atmosphere/contents/[-GAME-TITLE-ID-]/' will stay there.

For example, if you enable a mod with a file named 'mario', but there's already a file named 'mario' in the same spot within the '/atmosphere/contents/[-GAME-TITLE-ID-]/' folder, the 'mario' file for the mod enabled won't be used. The other 'mario' file that's already there will continue to be used.
